extracted.intended_audience: federal regulatory analysts, agency economists, and policy staff preparing regulatory impact analyses for U.S. federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing regulatory analyses (benefit-cost and related assessments) for proposed, interim, and final federal rules under OMB Circular A-4 (updated November 2023). Emphasizes analytic approach, scope, baseline choice, alternatives, quantification and monetization, distributional treatment, uncertainty, discounting, transfers, and presentation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction: use accompanying Explanation and iterative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction highlights the accompanying 'Explanation and Response to Public Input' as a useful reference for analysts and clarifies key elements of a regulatory analysis, noting regulatory analysis is an iterative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysts should consult the Explanation and Response document and treat regulatory analysis as iterative—identifying and evaluating the need for regulatory action and refining analysis as new information becomes available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical approaches: favor BCA; CEA optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies Benefit-Cost Analysis (BCA) and Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA) as systematic frameworks but underscores that OMB encourages agencies to use BCA as the typically more informative analytical approach; CEA is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may use CEA in some contexts, but the final Circular removed explanatory text about when to prefer CEA; agencies should default to BCA when feasible and document rationale if using CEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of analysis: consider global effects and set temporal bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering costs and benefits, agencies should consider all relevant effects 'regardless of whether they result from a regulation’s domestic applicability, or from a regulation’s impact on foreign entities' and may include effects on U.S. citizens abroad and, in some cases, noncitizens abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conducting global analysis, provide a supplemental analysis of effects on U.S. citizens and residents unless impractical. Use the year regulation begins to have effects as the start point, and choose an end point far enough in the future to capture all benefits and costs relevant to policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing an analytic baseline: without-statute and with-statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Circular refers to 'without-statute' and 'with-statute' baselines (terminology changed from pre-/post-statute in the draft) and maintains flexibility for agencies to select appropriate baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and clearly describe the baseline scenario (without- or with-statute) and account for how changing future conditions could affect estimated benefits and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying potential needs for federal regulatory action
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory analysis should assess whether federal regulation is warranted by common potential needs such as externalities (expanded to include 'positional goods'), asymmetric or imperfect information (including principal-agent problems), and the need to improve government operations and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss types of market or institutional failures the regulation addresses; consider whether failure to act would reflect a failure of public institutions and whether federal action is the best approach compared to alternatives (e.g., state/local action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting and evaluating alternative regulatory approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider a reasonable set of alternatives (including nudges, market-based approaches, performance vs. design standards), but recognize practical limits to analyzing all combinations of provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages pilot projects and data collection to test alternatives; when comparing performance and design standards, analyze costs of assuring compliance, likely degrees of compliance, and net benefits; avoid blanket generalizations about which standard is cheaper. For market-based approaches, study measurability of targeted behavior, whether penalties/rewards induce real behavioral change, and monitoring/compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing benefits and costs: quantify and monetize where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Rename from 'Developing Benefit and Cost Estimates' to 'Assessing Benefits and Costs.' Focus on benefits and costs (references to transfers moved elsewhere), with expanded discussion of WTP and WTA methods and additional examples to illustrate valuation issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude costs that drive intermediate activities yielding later benefits or costs. Provide examples and partial-equilibrium contexts as appropriate. Document methods and choices for monetization; use stated-preference methods where useful and explain limits (e.g., when WTP may be incomplete).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating non-monetized and unquantified effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should explicitly address non-monetized or unquantified effects and present discussion and a summary table of important unquantified effects prominently in the analysis to facilitate policymaker and public consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the discussion and summary table prominently (e.g., executive summary) so unquantified effects meaningfully inform policy choice; explain why effects could not be monetized or quantified and their potential importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetizing health and safety benefits and costs (including QALYs, WTP/WTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Circular simplifies guidance on monetizing health and safety effects, mentions quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) as a way to monetize health effects, and continues to highlight the need to use appropriate methods and document choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document chosen valuation methods (e.g., WTP, WTA, QALYs). The Circular shortened literature summaries on contested topics (VSL, VSLY); when issues are unsettled, OMB expects agencies to document methods and consult OMB as needed in specific analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional benefits and costs (formerly 'ancillary benefits' and 'countervailing risks')
rubrics_metrics.description: Recharacterizes ancillary benefits/countervailing risks as 'additional benefits and costs' and clarifies that costs should not be excluded when they drive intermediate activities that create downstream benefits or costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in analysis effects that are intermediate inputs to later benefits/costs (e.g., information collection leading to future benefits) and document linkages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for compliance and take-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are encouraged to explain assumptions about compliance and how alternative regulatory approaches could affect compliance and administrative costs; explore distributional effects of uneven compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence suggests full compliance is unlikely but agency assumes full compliance, explain that assumption and analyze how realistic compliance strategies or design choices would change estimated benefits, costs, and distributional outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains two alternative approaches to accounting for transfers: (1) present transfers separately from benefits and costs, or (2) account for transfers as both benefits and costs. The final Circular deletes the statement that presenting transfers separately is the default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify groups that contribute to or receive transfers (not just who initially pays/receives) because ultimate welfare effects may differ; consider behavioral effects of transfers and, where appropriate, use market models for society-wide accounting of net benefits. Document chosen approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributional analyses and weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommends applying weights to benefits and costs to reflect distributional concerns using a constant-elasticity approach with an absolute income elasticity of marginal utility of 1.4 (agencies may use another estimate if justified). Agencies must still produce traditionally-weighted (unweighted) estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both traditionally-weighted and weighted estimates; do not treat weighted estimates as primary if they are less informative. Emphasize unit of analysis and granularity—more granular estimates improve informativeness of weighted analyses. Agencies retain discretion on when and which groups to analyze; a case-by-case approach is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of uncertainty and certainty-equivalent valuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes the presumption of risk neutrality from earlier guidance and assumes risk aversion in valuing uncertain outcomes; final Circular adds mathematical detail on estimating certainty-equivalent valuations and uses the same absolute elasticity of marginal utility (1.4) to value aversion to uncertainty and inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certainty-equivalent methods where appropriate and document risk assumptions and calculations. The additional mathematical detail clarifies how to calculate benefits and costs under different risk assumptions and how certainty-equivalent approaches affect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount rates: social rate of time preference and risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the default social rate of time preference at 2.0 percent (changed from 1.7%) by adopting a constant 0.3 percentage-point CPI–PCE differential adjustment; deletes discussion of the Ramsey approach; provides guidance on obtaining risk-adjusted discount rates to account for systematic risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default social rate = 2.0% (based on 10-year Treasury yields adjusted for PCE inflation). If accounting for systematic risk, agencies may use risk-adjusted discount rates by combining an economy-wide risk premium and the correlation of regulatory benefits/costs with systematic risk. Refer to Circular A-94 for methods to estimate risk-adjusted rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of results and accounting statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounting statement should be included 'preferably in an executive summary or otherwise in a prominent early place.' The suggested format now includes a row for 'Annualized monetized net benefits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow suggested accounting-statement format and include annualized monetized net benefits as a row. Place key summaries prominently to aid policymakers; ensure transparency about assumptions, ranges, and unquantified effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized analytical requirements: NEPA and environmental justice considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Section on specialized analytical requirements renamed subsections to 'National Environmental Policy Act' and 'Health and Environmental Impacts on Communities with Environmental Justice Concern' and references Executive Order 14096.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, incorporate NEPA-related analyses and assess health/environmental impacts on communities with environmental justice concerns consistent with Executive Order 14096 and related statutory requirements; use appropriate analytical methods and disclosure.
